note: Christmas Island: the Christmas Island Act 1958, s. 8A (Compilation No. 13, 18 December 2020, the latest legislation.gov.au lists), puts Western Australia's laws, as in force there from time to time, in force in the Territory, save as an Ordinance amends or suspends them; no Ordinance suspending the two WA Acts below was looked for, so their application is my reading of s. 8A. Majority: WA's Age of Majority Act 1972, s. 5 (compilation as at 22 August 2003, the current one the WA register serves): a person attains full age and full capacity at 18. Marriage doesn't change it; the form holds no contract consent rule. Work: WA's Children and Community Services Act 2004 (official version as at 15 October 2026), s. 190, bars employing a child under 15 in a business, trade or occupation carried on for profit; s. 191 excepts a family business, delivery work from 10 (accompanied, 6 a.m. to 7 p.m.) and shop, retail or restaurant work from 13 with a parent's written permission (6 a.m. to 10 p.m.), which the form doesn't hold. Performers: s. 191(2) excepts a child employed in a dramatic or musical performance or other entertainment or in making an advertisement, with no permit, so performers are free; s. 192 makes employing a child to perform indecently a crime, and s. 193 lets the CEO prohibit or limit a child's employment, neither held. Commonwealth workplace law on Christmas and Cocos isn't read. Service: Australia has no peacetime conscription. The Defence Act 1903 (Compilation No. 88, 29 September 2026), which extends to the external Territories (s. 5A), makes residents of 18 to 59 who have lived in Australia six months liable to serve only when the Governor-General calls them by proclamation in time of war, approved by both Houses (ss. 59-60); so service is none, the wartime liability not held.
